translationRepairs: They treated him as a puppet, letting him have his way in trifles while never truly minding what he did.
Yet Chong and the others treated him like a small child; in a hundred affairs he had a free hand, and at first they did not bother to restrain or keep a record of him.

視之如小兒 and 百事自由 mean Chong and the others treated Penzi as a child with a free hand in all affairs, not a puppet confined to trifles; 初不恤錄 is failure to supervise or keep a record, not mere indifference.
After Guangwu's death Prince Jing of Shanyang showed so little sorrow at the bier that he was suspected at once; he then sent a secret letter to the Prince of Donghai, goading him into revolt.
After Guangwu's death Prince Jing of Shanyang wept without grief; he composed a flying letter to the Prince of Donghai, urging him to rise in rebellion.

哭不哀 states only that Jing wept without grief; the original invents immediate suspicion and a bier scene, while 作飛書 is composing a flying letter, not a separately inferred secret plot after being suspected.

In the eighth year of that reign Emperor Huan seized on a solar eclipse as his cue, named the former minister Han Yin metropolitan commandant, and purged the eunuch faction step by step until Luoyang was clean again.

In the eighth year of that reign Emperor Huan seized on a solar eclipse as his cue, named the former Minister of Education Han Yin metropolitan commandant, and purged the eunuch faction step by step until Luoyang was clean again.
故司徒韩寅 is the former Minister of Education (司徒), not a generic former minister; the rest of the proposed sentence keeps the original wording while restoring that office.
He was proved right when the emperor came back from exile and the world slid into chaos.
Later he returned, and thereupon there was great disorder.
后還，遂大亂 names neither an emperor nor exile, and does not say Mo Si was proved right; the original invents subject, exile, and vindication.
An edict asked Master of Writing Cai Yong.
An edict asked the gentleman consultant Cai Yong.
詔以問議郎蔡邕 names Cai Yong as gentleman consultant (議郎), not Master of Writing (尚書); the idiomatic line already has the correct office.
When Emperor Ai died the empress regent installed Wang Mang's nephew as grand marshal—and chaos followed.
When Emperor Ai died, the empress held the regency; Wang Mang, the empress's elder brother's son, became grand marshal—and chaos followed.
王莽以后兄子爲大司馬 identifies Wang Mang himself as the empress's elder brother's son who became grand marshal; 'Wang Mang's nephew' inverts the kinship and invents a different appointee.
Xiang Kai argued that the academy had housed the ancient "doubtful" star; when its gate gave way of its own accord, it foretold the collapse of moral culture and the abandonment of education.

Xiang Kai argued that the Imperial Academy was where the Qianyi counselors had resided; when its gate gave way of its own accord, it foretold the collapse of moral culture and the abandonment of education.
前疑 is the ancient counselor office Qianyi, not a 'doubtful' star; the proposal is right to reject the star reading but wrongly splits 前 as 'former' before a romanized qianyi.
Four years later another parched summer arrived.
In the sixth year, summer, there was drought.
六年夏，旱 names the sixth year of the era; 'four years later' is not in the Chinese and, after the neighboring 三年 record, miscounts the interval.
When the boy emperor died, Li Gu the grand commandant begged Liang Ji to choose a mature, virtuous heir so the realm might rally and their own names live on.

When the boy emperor died, Grand Commandant Li Gu urged the empress dowager's brother Liang Ji to establish an heir-emperor, choosing one advanced in years and possessed of virtue, so that if all under Heaven relied on him their merit and fame would not perish.
太尉李固勸太后兄梁冀立嗣帝 names Liang Ji as the empress dowager's brother and asks him to establish an heir-emperor; the original drops 太后兄 and flattens 立嗣帝 and 功名不朽.
Shu was then executed and destroyed.
He was then executed and destroyed.
述遂誅滅 continues Gongsun Shu's given name 述 from 公孙述, not the region 蜀; the literal 'Shu was then executed' reads the person as a place.
The long train rolling toward Hejian foretold the emperor's death and the hearse-road that would bring the boy Liu Hong from Hejian to the throne.
The long train rolling toward Hejian foretold the emperor's death and the hearse-road that would bring Emperor Ling from Hejian to the throne.
迎靈帝 names Emperor Ling only; the personal name Liu Hong is not in this unit and was invented in the idiomatic English.
Coins for rooms and gold for halls pictured Lady Dong of Yongle hoarding metal to gild her halls once her son took the throne.
Coins for rooms and gold for halls pictured Empress Dowager Yongle hoarding metal to gild her halls once her son took the throne.
其母永樂太后 identifies Ling's mother by the Yongle empress-dowager title only; the surname Dong is not in this unit.

Eunuchs Guan Ba and Su Kang loathed upright scholars; with Liu Ao, Xu Yong, and Liu Fen—they formed a clique; Yuan Shansong's Book notes Liu Fen belonged to the power-broker faction impeached by Fan Pang.

Regular palace attendants Guan Ba and Su Kang loathed outstanding worthies of the realm; with the junior privy treasurer of Changle Liu Ao, the chamberlain for ceremonies Xu Yong, and the imperial secretary Liu Fen they formed a clique; Yuan Shansong's Book notes that Liu Fen belonged to the power-broker faction impeached by Fan Pang.
The original drops 中常侍, 長樂少府, 太常, and 尚書; the proposal restores those offices but over-renders 尚書 as secretariat director (尚書令).

In Zhongping 6 the young Liu Xie was hustled to the throne while his brother lacked even a princely rank; dozens of eunuchs led him off with the whole bureaucracy trailing until the party turned back only at the Yellow River.

In Zhongping 6 Marquis Shi mounted the supreme seat; Emperor Xian still had no noble title. He was seized by palace attendant Duan Gui and several tens of others; the dukes, ministers, and all officials followed, and only when they reached the river could they return.
史侯登蹑至尊 is Marquis Shi's accession; 獻帝未有爵號 is Emperor Xian still without a noble title, and 中常侍段珪 names Duan Gui. The original wrongly seats Liu Xie on the throne.
"Begins to decline" foretold Lady Cai's death and the scattering of Biao's generals.
"When it first declines" means Liu Biao's wife was about to die, and the various generals would fall away and scatter.
劉表妻當死 names only Liu Biao's wife; Lady Cai is an identification not present in this unit.
The thirteenth year marked Liu Biao's own end and the people's removal toward the north under Cao Cao's Ji Province.
"By the thirteenth year not a sprig is left" means in the thirteenth year Biao too was about to die, and the people were about to move to Ji Province.
民當移詣冀州 says the people were to move to Ji Province; Cao Cao is not named, and 表又當死 is Biao's own coming death.
In Jian'an 3 Yuan Shao crushed him; Zan hanged his kin, set himself ablaze, and Shao's men stormed the tower to take his head.
In Jian'an 3 Yuan Shao attacked Zan; Zan was greatly defeated, strangled his sisters, wife, and children, set fire and burned himself; Shao's troops rushed up the tower and beheaded him.
袁紹攻瓚，瓚大敗，縊其姊妹妻子 names an attack, a great defeat, and strangling of sisters, wife, and children; 'hanged his kin' omits the defeat and collapses the kinship list.
